Judgment

1. Revisionist has filed the present revision petition against impugned order dated 14.08.2023,
passed by Ms. Himanshi Tyagi, Ld. MM-03, East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, whereby application of the complainant/revisionist herein under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.was dismissed.

2. The factual matrix of the case is that revisionist/ complainant had filed a complaint and application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. against respondent nos.2 & 3/accused persons, namely,
Kiran Thakur @ Reetu Soni and Neeraj @ Manoj, praying for registration of FIR against them for offences under Sections 420/468/471/506/34 IPC.
The case of the complainant/revisionist is that he is owner of Flat No. a-255, 3 rd Floor, G.D.Colony, Mayur Vihar, Phase-3, Delhi-110096.

Revisionist along with his wife and two daughters used to reside in the said flat and thereafter, he along with his wife shifted to flat no. 8, 3rd Floor, Khasra no.468/1, Jamaipura, Village Khora,
Ghaziabad and his daughters Priyanshi and Nandani continue to reside in the flat no. A-255, 3rd Floor, G.D.Colony Mayur Viharr Phase-3, Delhi.
The revisionist had locked the room in the said flat where his household articles, jewellery and some documents were lying, when he shifted to flat in Khora Colony.
Revisionist had some dispute with his daughters Priyanshi and Nandani and filed eviction petition against them before Hon'ble Senior Citizen Welfare Tribunal, Geeta Colony, Delhi.

entities.text: Senior Citizen Welfare Tribunal, Geeta Colony,

sentences.text:
It is stated that accused Crl. (R) 240/23 :: 3 ::
persons/respondent nos. 2 & 3 herein were residing at 2nd floor of the same property and they knew about the dispute between him and his daughters.

On 04.11.2022,
when the complainant reached at his flat no. A-255, G.D.Colony, Mayur Vihar, he found his articles missing and lock of the said room was broken.
He reported the matter to the Police.
Both the parties were called in the PS but no action was taken by the Police.
It is mentioned that accused persons had been threatening the complainant to kill and face dire consequences.
A complaint was made by the complainant to concerned SHO, on 05.11.2022, ACP, DCP & other authorities.
Thereafter, the complainant filed a complaint under Section 200 along with an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C.

Thereafter, the complainant received a legal notice dated 28.11.2022 on his whatsapp number on 29.11.2022 in which they claimed that complainant had executed registry of property in question in favour of respondent no.2 herein and they had entered into an agreement to sell dated 20.09.2022 and respondent no.3 herein had already paid an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- to the complainant.
It is mentioned that accused persons have prepared some false and fake documents in order to grab his property.
A written complaint dated 03.12.2022 was given to SHO, PS Gazipur and copy thereof was sent to DCP concerned and other higher authorities, but no action has been taken.

Hence,
a complaint along with application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was filed in Ld. Trial Court.

3. In the present case, action taken report was called from concerned Police Station wherein it was mentioned that alleged Crl. (R) 240/23 :: 4 ::

sentences.text:
After hearing Ld. Counsel for the complainant and considering the material available on record,
Ld. Trial Court came to the conclusion that facts of the case do not require registration of FIR, as identity of the accused is known to the complainant, all the facts and circumstances are within knowledge of complainant and evidence can be conveniently taken without assistance of Police investigation.
It was further observed that if there is any need, police inquiry can be held under Section 202 Cr.P.C.
therefore, application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was dismissed.

However, Ld.
Trial Court took cognizance of offence under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and fixed the case for pre-summoning evidence.
Hence, the present revision was filed.
5. Ld.

Counsel for the revisionist has submitted that proposed accused persons/ respondent nos. 2 &
3 herein took advantage of dispute between the revisionist and his daughters.
It is further submitted that respondent nos. 2 & 3 committed theft in respect of articles and documents of the revisionist.

He has further submitted that revisionist never sold the flat in question to respondent nos. 2 & 3,
nor did he execute any document in their favour.
It is submitted that facts of the complaint disclose commission of cognizable offences, therefore, FIR may be ordered to be registered in this case.
Ld. Counsel for the respondents has submitted that respondent no. 2 has purchased the flat in question from the revisionist against consideration.
It is further submitted that respondents have not committed any theft or forgery as alleged, as vacant and peaceful possession of the flat in question was handed over to respondent no.2.
It is prayed that there is no infirmity in the impugned order and revision is liable to be dismissed.
7. I have considered the submissions made by Ld. Counsel for the complainant, impugned order and perused the material available on record.

8. Considering the facts of the case in hand, also considering the law laid down in M/S. Skipper Beverages Pvt. Ltd. vs State, 2001 IV AD Delhi 625, I am of the opinion that present dispute between the parties appears to be civil in nature, being related to sale and purchase of a property.

Trial court had rightly held that there is no requirement of police investigation, as identity of accused is known to the complainant and all the facts and circumstances of the case are within knowledge of the complainant and evidence can be conveniently taken without assistance of police investigation.
Thus, there appears no requirement of police investigation.

It was further held that if there is any need, police inquiry can be had under section 202 Cr.P.C.
